description: Services emit logs and return values but no typed completion/state-change events Environment can subscribe to. Session effects rely on a git-poll adapter and invocation-result envelopes.
desired_contract: Typed, subscribable completion/state events per owning service.
effect: Poll-based sources only; provider push notification is not yet available.
evidence: mncs-environment/mncs_env/sources.py generic Source contract with live store-replay, git-heads, commons-sync, and language-service sources; no provider push bus found
title: No canonical provider event feeds
why_not_local: Event semantics belong to the owning services; an environment-local bus would become a competing standard.
workaround: Background reconciler polls typed sources with durable cursors and Store replay-across-downtime; subscriptions replay from the session log.

description: Nothing in MNCS records which agent owns a worktree or branch. Environment keeps a local advisory lease file enforced only inside its own authority evaluation.
desired_contract: Family lease record (holder, scope, expiry, release) readable without joining Environment.
effect: Cross-harness ownership is voluntary; Environment-side conflicts deny inside its own authority evaluation.
evidence: control/leases.py exists but is service-local; no family lease contract found
title: No canonical workspace lease/ownership mechanism
why_not_local: Cross-agent ownership must be authoritative family-wide; a local file cannot bind other harnesses.
workaround: claims v2 (repository/worktree/path scopes, conflict denial, dirty-adoption, liveness) + Control worktree surface; unknown work is never touched.

description: Session authority is projected from intent constraints and protected scopes. Canonical authorization semantics live in mncs-rights-provenance, which Environment does not yet bind.
effect: AuthorityContext is intent-declared; escalation paths are explicit but human-mediated.
evidence: No machine grant-check endpoint was consumable from survey
title: Rights/provenance granularity for session authority
why_not_local: Replacing rights evaluation would be security theater and a competing authorization universe.
workaround: Pure evaluate() with default-deny; every denial/escalation is an event.

description: Intent, authority projection, lifecycle, and checkpoints are JSON contracts over host infrastructure.
desired_contract: Stable file-effect + record-schema story for Environment projection inside MNCS.
effect: Canonical semantics live in Python with JSON contracts; migration path stays open.
title: Environment concepts have no native MNCS representation yet
why_not_local: Forcing immature language features would block useful infrastructure for ideological purity.
workaround: JSON contracts are canonical; host code is transport/discovery only.

description: Real entry discovers Forge resident-entry and process-supervision contracts, but its manifests supply fingerprint sources rather than callable invocation descriptors. Treating those files as executable commands advertised unavailable tools as available. Atlas context also has older fingerprint-only metadata.
desired_contract: Provider-declared fixed invocation argv/effects for read-only status and idempotent reconciliation, stable response schema, readiness fields, workspace identity, and bounded recovery. Atlas should publish its existing context invocation.
effect: Forge resident availability is not verified or automatically started by standard Environment entry; unsupported provider contracts remain discoverable with actionable diagnostics.
evidence: Forge .mncs/project.json revision 7 workspace-first-continuous-entry and continuous-process-supervision; Forge continuous.environment_enter already starts/reuses services and queries family_agent_context; dogfood selected entry reports Forge contracts as provider-invocation-undeclared. Atlas context-capsule uses registry/__main__.py through the explicit bootstrap adapter.
title: Provider evidence is not invocation or readiness addressing
why_not_local: Provider effects, startup semantics, process identity, JSON status meaning, and the correct CLI belong to the provider. Executing evidence modules would guess a protocol and can falsely report success.
workaround: Environment composes explicitly declared service probes/reconciliation under session authority; source fingerprints stay noncallable. The proven Atlas orientation adapter is retained in the small bootstrap table.

description: Entry observes a Language checkout revision and binds its exact release/debug executable, but file presence and executable permissions cannot establish which revision produced that binary or which runtime/features it actually supports. Selected native Test invocation passed, but that does not prove every bound toolchain operation.
desired_contract: Bounded provider-owned JSON toolchain inspection including binary build revision, compiler/runtime/schema versions, feature identities, and an actual readiness sentinel; status/reconciliation invocation declarations for Environment.
effect: Toolchain status is availability, not proof of source/binary compatibility. Native invocation proves the exercised capability only.
evidence: Dogfood session binds mncs-language/target/release/mncs, records observed checkout HEAD, and invokes mncs.test-result/1 successfully. CLI declarations separately select target/debug/mncs for several capabilities; no build-info/toolchain-info surface was found in crates/mncs-cli/src/main.rs.
title: Compiler executable cannot be tied to observed checkout readiness
why_not_local: Environment cannot infer compiler build provenance from Git HEAD or implement compiler/runtime feature semantics. Calling a binary present must remain a substrate observation.
workaround: Bind selected paths without ambient compiler fallback, probe permissions/toolchain presence, expose the verification basis, and exercise native provider contracts explicitly.

description: The existing background reconciler tests os.kill(pid, 0) against a PID file. A reused unrelated live PID can appear to be the reconciler; simultaneous daemon starts can race between checking and writing the PID file.
desired_contract: Exclusive daemon ownership lock plus process start identity and bounded heartbeat/readiness; consume the provider process-supervision contract for externally owned services.
effect: Background daemon PID status is not a verified service-readiness observation. Foreground health and declared provider probes are the canonical entry readiness checks.
evidence: mncs_env/reconciler.py Daemon.run and Daemon.status. This run added locking for foreground entry/reconciliation and workspace-scoped reconciler session selection, but did not launch or replace existing daemons.
owner: mncs-environment (follow-up); mncs-control / mncs-forge for reusable supervision contract
title: Environment reconciler process identity remains PID based
why_not_local: Environment owns hardening its own daemon, but should consume provider supervision for external services rather than create another general process supervisor.
workaround: Use foreground reconcile for deterministic entry recovery; do not kill or trust unrelated processes based on stale PID files.

description: Opening the canonical Store backend (EmbeddedStore construction plus verification) costs ~1.6s per process even before any read. Every mncs-env command pays it at least once, so entry/health/status latency is dominated by open cost rather than the work itself.
desired_contract: Sub-100ms Store open, or a documented persistent local handle / cheap generation probe that read-only commands can use without a full open.
effect: All store-backed commands take seconds; polling loops (status/health) are expensive.
evidence: mncs-environment session open measured at 1.6-1.9s with and without verify_on_open; entry paid it twice per invocation before the single-open change
title: Store open cost dominates every CLI command
why_not_local: Persistence lifecycle and verification live inside mncs-store; Environment cannot safely cache across processes without a store-owned handle or generation feed.
workaround: Single store open per entry; no-store file-side epoch fast path for status --terse; validated health epochs skip redundant revalidation and probes.

description: Providers publish diagnostics and invocation descriptors, but no family contract names a remediation capability (observe/repair/validate/envelope). Each orchestrator-to-provider remediation binding is currently a bilateral convention.
desired_contract: Family remediation capability shape: discovery suffix or manifest kind, argv/JSON envelope schema, effects/authority expectations, evidence routing (session artifact dir).
effect: Only mncs-doctor exposes remediation; other providers cannot be orchestrated until they adopt the bilateral convention.
evidence: mncs-environment/mncs_env/doctor.py defines the :repository-remediation suffix convention and consumes the mncs.doctor.remediation/1 envelope bilaterally with mncs-doctor
title: No family-standard remediation capability contract
why_not_local: A family capability contract must be standardized where providers coordinate; an Environment-only standard would fork the vocabulary.
